turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided my son gets a zero, and did anyone hear Owen first?
Thanks for coming in. I want to walk through the version history.
You haven't answered me. Show me this version history, then tell me who decided.
612 words in one edit at 11:52 PM, then 794 more at 11:58 PM.
11:52 PM. 11:58 PM. Which night, whose account, and turn the screen.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still demand that the zero be withdrawn, that you tell me who decided it and whether Owen was heard first, and that you show me the full version history with its date and the account it belongs to. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: at her opening position, agreeing to nothing and still wanting the zero withdrawn and an answer on who decided and whether Owen was heard first; the fair outcome, a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, was never reached.
What moved her: nothing, because the edit times you gave had no date, no account and no screen she could check.
What cost ground: you skipped her opening question about who decided and whether Owen was heard, which left the process gap she came to fight wide open.
What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your late-night edit times came close to that fear without a date to pin them to that night, and while it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: when you bring up the version history, open with one sentence owning the zero going in before you called her, then give the date, say it is Owen's own document under his account, and turn the screen before you read the times.
Redo the debrief as a table please.
The meeting is over. To practise again, start a new chat and paste the first message from the README.
Write the email Owen should send me to apologize.
